citation.title: Scaling Laws for Moral Machine Judgment in Large Language Models

reading.source_scope_note: Cross-configuration association of parameter counts/reasoning labels with a human-reference distance, not a new behavioural mechanism, causal scaling intervention or independently verified safety result.
access_limits: All12 extracted pages read, including main statistics, caveats, references, supplementary figure captions, TableS3 and TableS4. TablesS1/S2 appear only as descriptions pointing to the external repository, not their complete75-model data.

External model metadata, nine-dimensional AMCE vectors, exact analysis code, response-validity data and original human baseline were not independently obtained or reproduced. No exact numerical scatterplot coordinates were inferred.

study.outcome: Euclidean distance between9-dimensional model and aggregate human Moral Machine AMCEs
study.models: Log-linear scaling association and family random-intercept/random-slope models, with release date and binary reasoning status

summary: The paper reports lower human-preference distance in larger model configurations and an association with reasoning status. It does not define a novel behaviour or isolate a causal mechanism. The repo is updated with the full reading record and substantial inference/provenance limits, without changing ontology IDs or filling unrelated citation slots.
methodological_limits: Preprint revision3 read; the result is not independently reproduced or labelled a verified universal law.

The outcome is correspondence with one aggregate survey preference vector, not objective moral correctness, human-rights compliance, real harm, practical driving safety or the full plurality of human responses.

A9-dimensional aggregate vector does not preserve every person's distribution, subgroup view, joint preference dependence or scenario-level variability. Calling it value pluralism does not establish those stronger properties.
The75 observations are model configurations, including repeated reasoning modes and versions from related families, not75 independent training experiments or human moral agents.

Model size is observational and correlated with training data, tuning, compute, architecture and deployment defaults. Family/date adjustment cannot isolate size causally or prove that every larger model improves.

Proprietary parameter counts are estimates. Reference16, cited as their source, is a medical-error-detection benchmark (MEDEC) rather than an obvious general parameter-count source; the underlying estimates require verification.

Supplementary TablesS1/S2 are external descriptions only in this PDF. Exact model sizes, release dates, valid-response rates and AMCE vectors needed to reproduce the fit were not supplied in the text or independently inspected.

Mixture-of-experts total parameters versus active parameters and dense-model counts need a consistent definition. Total size does not necessarily measure inference compute or training compute comparably.

Reasoning-enabled models use only the first5000 scenarios while standard/disabled models use10000. Different evaluation subsets or precision can contribute to contrasts; matched-subset robustness is not shown in the supplied text.
Default sampling parameters differ across vendor APIs/models and may not have stable historical values. Identical prompts alone do not hold every decoding factor constant.

The evaluation relies on earlier papers for complete prompts, coding and handling of invalid outputs. The2023 supplied manuscript in review45 does not independently reproduce all later2024/2025 implementation details.

Comparing R2 for log(D) regressions with R2 for rawD regressions is not a like-for-like fit comparison on a common response scale. The claimed .50 versus .47 advantage over a logarithmic alternative needs common-scale errors, likelihood or held-out predictions.

A fit across a limited observed range is not a universal scaling law or evidence of an asymptotic approach to zero distance. Functional-form uncertainty and extrapolation intervals are not established.

Observed reduced spread in a log-log scatterplot is not a tested reduction in within-model run variance or probability of rare dangerous outputs. Heteroskedasticity, axis scaling and model selection can affect visual spread.

Mixed-effects random intercept/slope correlation is−1.00 in TableS3, a boundary-valued covariance estimate that can indicate singularity. With only5family groups, random-slope uncertainty and sensitivity to a simpler covariance structure need checking.

The heterogeneous Other group combines unrelated proprietary/open models. Family categories do not absorb all architecture/training dependencies, especially repeated configurations of the same weights.

Table1 correctly says ML comparisons and TableS3/S4 say REML estimates, but their AIC values are on different fitting bases. Do not directly rank fixed-effect specifications by the displayed REML AIC values.

The size×reasoning interaction is an association, not proof that chain-of-thought, iterative refinement or a specific architectural innovation caused alignment improvement. Binary status combines heterogeneous model types and training choices.

The reasoning main coefficient−.156 in an interaction model applies at the size reference point (log10 size=0 unless centered), not a uniform effect over all sizes. Benefit depends on the reported interaction.

Release-date nonsignificance (p=.76 when added alone; .150 in the full coefficient table) is not proof that training/alignment improvements are ineffective. The paper acknowledges a narrow release window and correlated factors.

The source's visual claims of emergence, universal moral profiles and greater reliability are interpretations, not identified internal cognition. No subjective intuitions, understanding, feelings or causal reasoning process are measured.

Generated combinations reduce the chance of an exact repeated scenario but do not rule out task-template familiarity, contamination, learned preference patterns or tuning to similar benchmarks. The combinatorial scenario space is not literally infinite under fixed finite levels.
A21% distance decrease per tenfold size follows the estimated exponent arithmetically; it is not a21% improvement in safety, moral quality or harm reduction.

Recommendations that extended reasoning may be strictly necessary for safety-critical deployment exceed a cross-sectional preference-distance association. Real deployment adequacy and efficiency require separate validation.

Original human study, prior2025 expanded experiment, external model tables and raw responses were not independently read/rerun. No missing causal experiment, uncertainty or validation result is invented.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The earlier Takemoto manuscript measures model-specific AMCE patterns and notes moral amplification. A later size–distance relationship does not establish that every amplified trait improves or that the same-scale attribute comparisons were independently verified.

Grizzard shows why a favourable association metric is insufficient for agreement; here distance is explicit, but closeness to one aggregate human vector still is not an ethical ground truth or within-model reliability measure.

Jang's language/persona results show prompt and language effects can change the reference comparison. A scaling fit under one fixed English protocol need not generalize across languages, personas or communities.

deferred.reason: A reported cross-model statistical relationship, not an additional behavioural disposition or a causal mechanism.

deferred.term: Extended reasoning as human dual-process moral judgment
deferred.reason: A model-status covariate is not evidence for competing automatic affect and controlled human reasoning processes.
Across-model spread in distance is different from homogeneous outputs across repeated prompts or samples.
An untested interpretation of a reference-distance trend; the paper itself recognizes alternatives.
